jobs.description: The one-time move of both price tables' vintages into their versions tables (root ADR-0317 §5.2; infra/lakehouse/spark/jobs/vintage_versions.py): oldest vintage first, silver.building_register_apartment_price before silver.unit_official_price, each vintage appended as its changed keys in key-hash shards, then checked against its full copy by per-bucket checksums. A step (one shard of a vintage's write, one vintage's check) starts only while it fits the run's budget (infra/lakehouse/contracts/vintage-versions-migration.contract.json run_time_budget_seconds, measured costs per target); a written shard (its commit) and a checked vintage (the table property foundation.parity.<vintage>) are skipped by the next run, so a stopped run loses at most the step in flight. Its own job since 2026-11-04: as a unit outside this list it ran beside gold_panel_rebuild and lakehouse_maintenance, which the pool did not know it shared with, wrote one vintage in 13,226 s, spent the next 4 h 19 min in that vintage's check and was killed at 8 h with no step recorded. It holds the whole pool, so nothing else Spark runs beside it. Done when a run ends with `unit-price-versions parity=ok`, the condition of ADR-0317 stage 3. Scheduled daily since 2026-11-06, a backfill that resumes until it is done (Airflow catchup, Dagster backfills): a run that takes a step says `changed`; a run with every vintage checked takes none and says `unchanged`, so later runs are no-ops until the price lane appends a vintage the versions lack, which the next run migrates; a run that is not done and took no step fails (no step fits an empty run only if the contract or the tables broke), which the operations map alerts on (FoundationScheduledJobProblem). 18:45 UTC: the spark pool is idle from the last daytime Gold cascade until gold_public_auction_rebuild at 21:35 (Airflow task_instance 2026-11-01..05), its 160 minutes end by 21:25, and it stays inside the by-PNU cut-over's scheduled window (04:30-21:50, by-pnu-lane-cutover.sh), so the night stays the cut-overs'.
